t: Listen to a talk in an economics class.
Every choice has a hidden price.
Economists call it opportunity cost: the value of the best alternative you give up.
Say you have a free Saturday.
You could work a shift and earn eighty dollars, or you could go hiking with friends.
If you go hiking, the hike isn't free.
Its opportunity cost is the eighty dollars you didn't earn.
A bakery that uses its oven for bread can't use that oven, at that hour, for cakes.
Opportunity cost is like the road not taken in a journey.
You never see it on the map of where you went, but it shaped every turn.
That's why good decisions compare options, not just prices.
